blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. This section was written from City of Chilliwack, School District 33, BC Transit and Chilliwack Museum pages, and replaces text that was repeated on the other Sardis guides.
How the Evans and Unsworth corridors came to be

Sardis sits on the traditional, unceded territory of the Stó:lō people. The City’s Sardis Neighbourhood Plan says the Ts’elxwéyeqw Tribe has lived here for thousands of years, and that mid-19th-century settlers came to farm, mostly dairy and hops.

Unsworth Road has the longer paper trail. The City's Trail Network Plan says the old New Westminster to Yale wagon road turned north after crossing Vedder Creek and ran along what is now Unsworth Road before reaching the small settlement then called Centerville. The Chilliwack Museum records that A.C. Wells settled a farm in Sardis in 1865, and that five generations of the Evans family have lived on a farm off Yale Road West, where a log cabin thought to date from the early 1860s still stands.

blocks.text: Getting around: Vedder Road is the spine

The Sardis plan calls Vedder Road the north-south spine of Sardis and says a frequent bus line with 15-minute service runs along it to downtown and the Canada Education Park. BC Transit's current Rider's Guide lists route 51 Vedder and route 66 FVX at the Vedder Road and Luckakuck Way stop. Route 52 Evans has separate weekday, Saturday, and Sunday and holiday timetables, with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Evans Road at Yale Road, Ashwell Road at Hodgins Avenue and downtown.

Two changes are on the City’s list: a Vedder Road corridor plan with wider sidewalks, street trees and better crossings, and a transit exchange next to Luckakuck Way. The Trail Network Plan also proposes a rail trail linking Sardis, Yarrow and Greendale with downtown. None is built yet, so treat them as direction, not a promise.
Schools, parks and trails nearby

Evans Elementary is at 7600 Evans Road (604-858-3057) and Unsworth Elementary is at 5685 Unsworth Road (604-858-4510). School District 33 sets catchments by address, so check the exact home with its school locator before you write an offer.
The Sardis plan lists Sardis Park, Sardis Sports Fields, Wells Landing Park, Manuel Park and Roy Park as existing Sardis parks.

blocks.text: What the plan means for buyers and owners

The plan says no vacant greenfield land is left in Sardis, so growth will come from infill and redevelopment, bounded by Highway 1, the ALR and the Vedder neighbourhood. It estimates Sardis will need roughly 1,300 to 1,700 more attached homes and 1,100 to 1,700 apartment units by 2041. Urban residential land allows houses, duplexes and accessory dwellings up to 10 m high; townhouses belong within about a ten-minute walk of services, and apartments of up to six storeys near frequent transit.

For a larger or combined lot, the plan expects redevelopment at higher density, and for a standard lot a split into two smaller lots. Along Evans Road the picture is different: the plan describes West Evans as ALR land between Stevenson and Evans roads, and says changing the urban boundary there would take talks with the Agricultural Land Commission. The City's small-scale housing guide (updated September 2024) allows up to three or four units on eligible lots. They must be inside the urban growth boundary, under 4,050 square metres, on City water and sewer, and in a listed zone. A secondary suite is allowed in any single detached home, needs a building permit, and cannot sit below the flood construction level.
Before you pay for a lot on the strength of what a neighbour built, ask Planning (604-793-2906) for its zone and plan designation.
Water and flood questions to ask

The City's drinking water comes from the Sardis-Vedder Aquifer, which lies north of the Vedder River and reaches up to Highway 1. The City says the water table is 5 to 10 metres down, the soil above it is coarse and very permeable, and its wells draw from 30 to 40 metres. So spills on the surface can reach it quickly. If the home has an old oil tank or a private well, ask about both.

Flooding is different by lot. The City says Vedder River floods are mostly fall and winter events that last 1 to 2 days, and that provincial dyke standards use a 1-in-200-year flood. Bylaw 4519 sets setbacks of 75 m from the Vedder River and 30 m from the Vedder Canal and Chilliwack River. The plan adds that the northern part of Sardis lies in the Fraser River floodplain, where buildings must be floodproofed. Call the Flood Information Line at 604-793-2757 with the exact address before you rely on a general map.
Condo buildings in Sardis West Vedder
First-coverage and position note. The area's condo shelf is a 55+ low-rise cluster on Knight Road and Amber Drive.
Knight Lodge — 45660 Knight Road

A 55+ apartment-condo building: current listings record sub-type Apartment/Condo, built 1989, in Sardis West Vedder, described as a welcoming 55+ / adult-oriented community with guest suite, workshop, games room, secure covered/underground parking and in-suite laundry. Published pet position (current listing aggregator): Cats OK, No Dogs, number limit one, with restrictions — listing-level data, not a bylaw summary.
Cotton Ridge — 45645 Knight Road

A 55+ apartment-condo building: current listings record sub-type Apartment/Condo, built 2006, in Sardis West Vedder, described as a sought-after 55+ condo with exercise centre, recreation facilities, library, guest suite and underground parking. Published restrictions (current listing): 55+ age restrictions, 2 pets allowed, "rentals allowed" — the rental position needs no bylaw since November 24, 2022; the pet and age positions are listing-level data, confirm on the Form B.
Morningside — 45520 Knight Road

An apartment-condo building: a current listing records sub-type Apartment/Condo, subdivision name Morningside, built 1995, in Sardis West Vedder, with guest suite, library, secure underground parking and in-suite laundry. Published pet position (current listing): small dogs and cats allowed, maximum 2 pets, with restrictions — listing-level data. Year note: the current listing states 1995; an older record for the same address conflicts.
Unnamed building — 7651 Amber Drive

A separate apartment-condo building two doors from The Sapphire: a current listing records sub-type Apartment/Condo, built 1992, in Sardis West Vedder, described in the listing text as one of Sardis' 55+ stratas, with gym, workshop, guest suite and recreation centre, wood-frame construction. The building is listed separately by address and should not be named as The Sapphire or merged with 7685 Amber Drive; a buyer must identify it by civic address and strata plan on the Form B.
Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Plan frame: the whole of Sardis sits inside the Schedule B5 Sardis Neighbourhood Plan area of the 2050 OCP (Bylaw 2025, No. 5500); the Agricultural Plan is Schedule B1 of the same bylaw and Schedule D is the Development Permit Areas schedule.

Where the condo stock concentrates: the Knight Road / Amber Drive pocket in central Sardis — five known apartment buildings within a short walk of each other (three on Knight Road, two on Amber Drive), four of them published as 55+ communities. The Evans Road corridor west of it holds the area's cross-referenced building and its pad-rental park.
Graham Secondary" and "Mt. Slesse Middle" — the Ministry forms above govern.

Catchments: SD33 catchments are address-based. One recorded locator run exists for this area's Evans Road corridor — 7600 Evans Road returned Evans Elementary, Vedder Middle School and Sardis Secondary, for that address only.

Transit: BC Transit Route 52 Evans runs between Cottonwood Mall and downtown Chilliwack via Evans Road and Yale Road, and Route 66 Fraser Valley Express serves Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Langley and Burnaby with daily service.

Two buildings, one street name, no shared name. Amber Drive holds The Sapphire (7685) and a second, unnamed 55+ building (7651) with a different build year and different amenity set — listing feeds blur them into one "Amber Drive condo" shelf, and only the civic address separates them.
The Sapphire's build year is genuinely conflicted. Current listings for the same building state 1992 and 1994.
Graham Secondary," "Mt. Slesse Middle").

There is no City recreation centre or park facility inside this sub-area on the directories the guide read — the nearest City recreation facility is the Sardis Sports Complex (5725 Tyson Road) in Sardis South, and the Sardis Library is at 5819 Tyson Road; both are a drive, not a walk, from the Knight Road cluster.
The 55+ cluster is also the area's oldest strata stock. Build years run 1989 (Knight Lodge) to 2006 (Cotton Ridge).

Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Chilliwack is not one of the 14 SnapStats-covered communities and CADREB publishes statistics board-wide only, with no sub-area tables.

Family townhouses hide in a seniors directory. Kiwanis Place (7760 Luckakuck Way) appears in seniors-housing directories because its operator is a housing society, but it is 34 units of family townhouses for families with children under 19 — the opposite of a 55+ complex — and it is non-market housing, not a purchasable townhouse complex.

There are no market statistics to quote for this sub-area — from anyone. CADREB publishes board-wide figures only and SnapStats does not cover Chilliwack, so any Sardis West Vedder "median price" a seller or a website offers is not coming from a published board or SnapStats source. Price from the property's own CADREB comparables.

items.t: "Sardis West Vedder" is an MLS® sub-area name in the City of Chilliwack for the part of Sardis west of Vedder Road. The closest official descriptions are the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, which covers Sardis as a whole, and the South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan, which names Vedder Road as its western boundary.
A feed count is a snapshot, not a land inventory.
Nearby areas: Sardis East Vedder and Promontory east of Vedder Road, Chilliwack Proper north of Highway 1, Vedder Crossing and Garrison Crossing to the south, and Cultus Lake further south.
How people search for it: "Sardis West Vedder homes for sale," "Sardis Chilliwack homes," "Evans Road Chilliwack homes," "Unsworth Road Chilliwack homes," "west of Vedder Road Sardis."

The Knight Road pair is really a pair (Nov 1, 2026). Knight Lodge (45660 Knight Rd, built 1989) and Cotton Ridge (45645 Knight Rd, built 2006) are neighbouring civic addresses on the same street — two separate 55+ strata buildings a short walk apart — and Amber Drive works the same way: The Sapphire (7685 Amber Dr) and the unnamed 55+ building at 7651 Amber Dr sit on the same short street west of Vedder Road.

Knight Road is filed on both sides of the Vedder Road divider. 45660 and 45645 Knight Road are labelled "Sardis West Vedder," while a listing at 45918 Knight Road (Country Park Village, Sardis East Vedder ground) is labelled "Sardis East Vedder" — the same street filed on both sides of the divider in board data. Filter by address, not by sub-area label.

faq.a: BC Transit’s route 52 Evans has weekday, Saturday, and Sunday and holiday timetables, with timing points at Cottonwood Mall, Evans Road at Yale Road, Ashwell Road at Hodgins Avenue and downtown. The Rider’s Guide gives no frequency, so check the timetable for your hours.
faq.q: Is there a bus on Evans Road?

faq.a: A secondary suite is allowed in any single detached house, with a building permit. Up to three or four units are possible on eligible lots under the City’s small-scale housing rules: inside the urban growth boundary, on City water and sewer, under 4,050 square metres and in a listed zone. Ask Planning about the exact lot.
faq.q: Can I add a suite or build more than one home on my lot?

faq.a: The City says the larger floods happen in fall and winter, usually last 1 to 2 days, and give little warning. It keeps a yearly-reviewed flood response plan for the Vedder. Flood construction levels and setbacks come from the Floodplain Regulation Bylaw, and apply lot by lot.
faq.q: What are the Vedder River floods like?

faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is set parcel by parcel. The Sardis plan treats the land between Stevenson Road and Evans Road as ALR. Look up any larger lot on the Agricultural Land Commission map before you plan to build or subdivide.
faq.q: Is any of Sardis West Vedder farmland?
